theory.title: Exercise 2.4.1: Basic FOR Loop
theory.content:
🔁 The Power of Iteration

MENTOR-9: "PROTO-7, checking systems one by one works... but what if you had 1000 systems?"

"FOR loops are the automation superpower. Write the check ONCE, iterate through ANY number of systems."

📘 FOR Loop Basics

Syntax:

FOR    ${variable}    IN    @{list}
    # Body (indented)
    Log    Processing ${variable}
END
  • FOR - Loop keyword (starts iteration)
  • ${variable} - Loop variable (changes each iteration)
  • IN - Separator keyword
  • @{list} - Collection to iterate
  • END - Closes the loop

💡 How It Works

@{systems}=    Create List    power    sensors    navigation

FOR    ${system}    IN    @{systems}
    Log    Checking ${system} system
END

# Iteration 1: ${system} = 'power' → Log "Checking power system"
# Iteration 2: ${system} = 'sensors' → Log "Checking sensors system"
# Iteration 3: ${system} = 'navigation' → Log "Checking navigation system"

⚙️ Key Rules

  • 🔹 Indentation matters: Loop body MUST be indented (4 spaces recommended)
  • 🔹 END alignment: END must align with FOR (same indentation)
  • 🔹 Loop variable scope: ${system} only exists inside the loop
  • 🔹 Empty lists: Loop skips if list is empty (0 iterations)

🎯 Your Task

Create a FOR loop that checks three systems: power, sensors, and navigation. One loop, three iterations!
